section: Economic reforms of 1991 - background, stabilisation and structural adjustment measures
subsections: Liberalisation measures - delicensing, MRTP, interest rates, trade
Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors
Criticism - jobless growth, crony capitalism, agrarian neglect

accepted.s:
Under the delicensing measures associated with the 1991 economic reforms, industrial licensing was abolished subject to exceptions relating to which of the following?
1. Hazardous chemicals
2. Aerospace
3. All agricultural activities
4. All information technology services
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Licensing was abolished except in a limited number of industries, including hazardous chemicals and aerospace. Agriculture and information technology services were not listed as the stated exceptions.
accepted.tq: Identify the limited exceptions and reject the over-broad additions.
accepted.sec: Liberalisation measures - delicensing, MRTP, interest rates, trade  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a direct consequence of industrial delicensing under the 1991 reforms?
o: Firms received freedom in pricing and faced no curbs on expansion
Import quotas were increased for domestic producers
Expansion of industries remained subject to compulsory licensing
All public sector industries were transferred to private ownership
accepted.x: Delicensing removed restrictions on industrial expansion and gave firms greater freedom in pricing, except in the limited industries retained under licensing.
accepted.tq: Link the reform instrument with its immediate operational effect.
accepted.sec: Liberalisation measures - delicensing, MRTP, interest rates, trade  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
The Industrial Policy of 1991 changed the MRTP framework by removing which of the following?
1. Asset limits
2. Pre-entry restrictions
3. Controls on mergers and expansion
4. Statutory status of SEBI
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The 1991 Industrial Policy abolished MRTP asset limits, pre-entry restrictions and controls on mergers and expansion. SEBI’s statutory status was a separate financial-market reform.
accepted.tq: Separate reforms belonging to the same period but different policy areas.
accepted.sec: Liberalisation measures - delicensing, MRTP, interest rates, trade  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which committee is associated with interest-rate deregulation and the entry of private banks during the economic reforms?
accepted.x: The Narasimham Committee was associated with financial-sector reforms, including interest-rate deregulation and private banking.
accepted.tq: Use the committee-to-recommendation association.
accepted.sec: Liberalisation measures - delicensing, MRTP, interest rates, trade  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Following the financial-sector reforms, the Reserve Bank of India was expected to move primarily from the role of a regulator to that of a
accepted.x: The reform framework envisaged a shift in the RBI’s role from direct regulation towards facilitation of the financial system.
accepted.tq: Test the precise institutional role rather than a broad reform label.
accepted.sec: Liberalisation measures - delicensing, MRTP, interest rates, trade  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In which year did SEBI acquire statutory status?
accepted.x: SEBI became a statutory body in 1992 as part of the strengthening of India’s securities-market framework.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the statutory milestone from nearby reform years.
accepted.sec: Liberalisation measures - delicensing, MRTP, interest rates, trade  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding trade reforms associated with the 1991 measures:
1. Import licensing was almost abolished.
2. EXIM scrips were removed.
3. Import quotas were removed.
4. Industrial expansion continued to require MRTP asset-limit approval.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Import licensing was almost abolished and EXIM scrips and quotas were removed. MRTP asset limits were themselves abolished, making statement 4 false.
accepted.tq: Find the one statement that reverses a simultaneous liberalisation measure.
accepted.sec: Liberalisation measures - delicensing, MRTP, interest rates, trade  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I
(a) Delicensing
(b) MRTP reform
(c) Financial reform
(d) Trade reform

List-II
(i) Removal of EXIM scrips and quotas
(ii) Freedom in pricing and expansion
(iii) Removal of asset limits and merger controls
(iv) Interest-rate deregulation
accepted.x: Delicensing brought freedom in pricing and expansion; MRTP reform removed asset and merger controls; financial reform included interest-rate deregulation; trade reform removed EXIM scrips and quotas.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched reform measures.
accepted.sec: Liberalisation measures - delicensing, MRTP, interest rates, trade  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The sharp reduction in the list of industries reserved for the public sector in 1991 is known as
accepted.x: Dereservation means reducing the industries reserved for the public sector and opening them to private participation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly prefixed reform terms.
accepted.sec: Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes disinvestment of public sector undertakings?
o: Replacement of private firms by public enterprises
Sale of PSU equity to reduce public ownership and improve financial discipline
Transfer of all PSU assets to the Reserve Bank of India
Compulsory closure of every loss-making public enterprise
accepted.x: Disinvestment involves the sale of equity in public sector undertakings. Its stated aims include financial discipline, modernisation and attracting foreign direct investment.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy from its mechanism and stated objectives.
accepted.sec: Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following were stated objectives of disinvestment?
1. Financial discipline
2. Modernisation
3. Attraction of FDI
4. Restoration of compulsory industrial licensing
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Disinvestment aimed at financial discipline, modernisation and attracting FDI. Restoration of compulsory industrial licensing was not an objective.
accepted.tq: Use the objective list and reject the unrelated reversal of liberalisation.
accepted.sec: Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: When private buyers acquire more than 51 per cent of the equity of a public sector undertaking, which consequence follows?
o: Only the market value of the PSU changes
The undertaking is placed under BIFR
Ownership and management pass to the private buyers
The undertaking automatically becomes a Navratna
accepted.x: A private acquisition exceeding 51 per cent transfers ownership and management of the undertaking to the private buyers.
accepted.tq: Apply the controlling-share threshold to determine the institutional consequence.
accepted.sec: Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was set up primarily to
accepted.x: BIFR was established for the revival and rehabilitation of sick industrial units.
accepted.tq: Match the specialised institution with its stated function.
accepted.sec: Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Public sector autonomy through Memoranda of Understanding was associated with which reform measure?
accepted.x: Memoranda of Understanding were used to provide greater autonomy and accountability to public sector undertakings.
accepted.tq: Connect the administrative instrument with the institutional reform it supports.
accepted.sec: Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Navratna scheme covered nine public sector undertakings in 1996. The notes distinguish this from the 97 profit-making Miniratnas and the 2021 New PSE Policy.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related PSU classifications by number and year.
accepted.sec: Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The number of profit-making public sector undertakings identified as Miniratnas was
accepted.x: Miniratnas were identified as 97 profit-making public sector undertakings.
accepted.tq: Test the exact numerical distinction between Navratnas and Miniratnas.
accepted.sec: Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The New PSE Policy announced in 2021 was associated with which of the following?
o: Removal of PSU autonomy through Memoranda of Understanding
accepted.x: The New PSE Policy of 2021 emphasised strategic disinvestment in the context of Atmanirbhar Bharat.
accepted.tq: Use the policy-year and its defining reform together.
accepted.sec: Privatisation measures - dereservation, disinvestment, opening sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following best illustrates the criticism of crony capitalism?
o: Agricultural investment increases uniformly across regions
Small firms exclusively control public-sector disinvestment
All firms receive equal access to public resources
Gains are concentrated among large, politically connected firms
accepted.x: Crony capitalism is criticised because economic gains become concentrated among large firms with political connections.
accepted.tq: Recognise the concept through its distributional consequence.
accepted.sec: Criticism - jobless growth, crony capitalism, agrarian neglect  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements best captures the criticism of agrarian neglect after structural reforms?
1. Public investment in agriculture lagged.
2. SAP-type reforms dismantled some food-system supports in the Global South.
3. Agricultural public investment became the fastest-growing component of reform expenditure.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The criticism points to lagging public investment in agriculture and the dismantling of food-system supports in parts of the Global South. Statement 3 contradicts that criticism.
accepted.tq: Combine two related criticisms and reject the exaggerated reversal.
accepted.sec: Criticism - jobless growth, crony capitalism, agrarian neglect  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who coined the term ‘Washington Consensus’ in 1989?
accepted.x: The term Washington Consensus was coined by John Williamson in 1989.
accepted.tq: Test the author-year association directly.
accepted.sec: Criticism - jobless growth, crony capitalism, agrarian neglect  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is NOT included among the rules associated with the Washington Consensus?
1. Fiscal discipline
2. Tax reform
3. Trade and FDI liberalisation
4. Compulsory expansion of public-sector reservation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Fiscal discipline, tax reform, and trade and FDI liberalisation were among the Washington Consensus rules. Compulsory expansion of public-sector reservation was not one of them.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the recognised policy package.
accepted.sec: Criticism - jobless growth, crony capitalism, agrarian neglect  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following combinations correctly represents elements of the Washington Consensus?
1. Privatisation
2. Deregulation
3. Property rights
4. Expansion of import quotas
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Privatisation, deregulation and protection of property rights were among the ten rules associated with the Washington Consensus. Expansion of import quotas was not included.
accepted.tq: Use the policy-list approach and identify the item that reverses liberalisation.
accepted.sec: Criticism - jobless growth, crony capitalism, agrarian neglect  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the broad stages described as Reforms 1.0, Reforms 2.0 and the Reforms 3.0 debate?
o: DPI in 1991 → LPG from 2014 → Reforms 3.0 before 1991
LPG in 1991 → DPI from 2014 onwards → debate on Reforms 3.0
LPG in 2014 → DPI in 1991 → Reforms 3.0 in 2021
Strategic disinvestment in 1991 → LPG in 2014 → DPI before 1991
accepted.x: Reforms 1.0 refers to liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation in 1991; Reforms 2.0 refers to digital public infrastructure from 2014 onwards; Reforms 3.0 remains a debate.
accepted.tq: Arrange reform phases by their stated years and distinguishing themes.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Reforms 2.0 from 2014 onwards are associated with which set of initiatives?
o: Hazardous chemicals, aerospace, CAD and forex cover
MRTP, EXIM scrips, quotas and import licensing
DPI, UPI, Jan Dhan and DBT
accepted.x: The initiatives associated with Reforms 2.0 are digital public infrastructure, UPI, Jan Dhan and direct benefit transfer.
accepted.tq: Identify the reform phase from its characteristic policy instruments.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
The improvement in India’s Market Distortions Performance Index position was credited to which of the following?
1. GST
2. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
3. Trade facilitation
4. Restoration of import quotas
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: GST, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, and trade facilitation were credited with the improvement. Restoration of import quotas was not cited.
accepted.tq: Select the reforms that support market efficiency and reject the protectionist distractor.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: During the SAP era, the annual growth rate of the Global South is stated to have fallen from
accepted.x: The cited comparison records a decline in annual growth from 3.2 per cent to 0.7 per cent during the adjustment era.
accepted.tq: Check both the figures and the direction of movement.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which two global financial crises have been blamed, in the stated criticism, on the Washington Consensus?
accepted.x: The Washington Consensus has been criticised in connection with the 1997 and 2008 financial crises.
accepted.tq: Associate the criticised policy framework with the specified crisis years.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which comparison regarding India’s external position is correct?
o: Forex cover was two weeks in 1991 and over 11 months later
Forex cover remained two weeks throughout the reform period
Forex cover was over 11 months in 1991 and two weeks later
Forex cover was one month in 1991 and four months later
accepted.x: India’s foreign-exchange cover was only about two weeks in 1991, compared with more than 11 months in the later comparison.
accepted.tq: Compare the historical crisis position with the later reserve position.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The current account deficit was 0.8 per cent of GDP in which period mentioned in the Economic Survey 2025–26 comparison?
accepted.x: The current account deficit was cited as 0.8 per cent of GDP in the first half of financial year 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Match the exact percentage with the specified accounting period.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: According to the cited comparison, India’s current account deficit peaked at 4.8 per cent of GDP in
accepted.x: The current account deficit peaked at 4.8 per cent of GDP in FY13.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the peak-year figure from the later deficit figure.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Persistent current account deficit has been identified as the structural cause of India’s
accepted.x: Persistent CAD has been identified as a structural cause of India’s high cost of capital.
accepted.tq: Connect the macroeconomic indicator with its stated structural consequence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In May 2026, the appeal to reduce consumption of fuel, gold and foreign travel was primarily intended to
o: increase imports and widen the trade deficit
accepted.x: The appeal sought to conserve foreign exchange by reducing expenditure on fuel, gold and foreign travel. It was described as an appeal not made even during 1991, when reserves were under $1 billion.
accepted.tq: Infer the macroeconomic objective from the items targeted for reduction.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: During the 1991 crisis, India’s foreign-exchange reserves were stated to be
accepted.x: The reserves were under $1 billion during the 1991 crisis.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the crisis-era reserve figure from later fund and oil-shock figures.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Economic Stabilisation Fund set up after the $100-per-barrel oil shock from the West Asia conflict amounted to
accepted.x: The Centre established an Economic Stabilisation Fund of ₹57,381 crore following the stated oil shock.
accepted.tq: Match the precise fund amount with the event that prompted it.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the broader significance attributed to the post-reform Indian economy?
o: It replaced all private investment with foreign aid
It moved towards enhanced global integration and a larger private sector
It restored universal industrial licensing and public-sector monopoly
It moved towards complete economic isolation and a smaller private sector
accepted.x: The post-reform economy is characterised by greater global integration and an expanded role for the private sector.
accepted.tq: Select the balanced long-term outcome rather than an absolute reversal.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
